name: Schattwald
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny village in the Tannheimer Tal with the Schattwald ski area and a natural outdoor pool.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Schattwald is located in the Außerfern region within the Reutte district at an altitude of 1,072 metres at the western end of the Tannheimer Tal valley, home to around 450 residents. Resting directly on the Bavarian border at the foot of Mount Wannenjoch (1,852 m), the village is framed by imposing alpine summits such as the Bschießer (2,000 m) and the Ponten (2,045 m). Schattwald is celebrated as the most tranquil retreat in the high valley, dedicated to peaceful nature tourism. Despite its name implying shade, the broad valley floor enjoys abundant sunshine and benefits from reliable snow conditions in winter and crisp alpine air in summer.

Geschichte

Bronze Age spearheads and Roman silver coins indicate that the mountain pass served as a trade route long before permanent settlement. Around 1300, Alemannic settlers from the adjacent Allgäu Ostrach valley cleared the land. Schattwald was first officially documented in 1432 under the name Schadwald when Duke Frederick IV of Tyrol acquired local landholdings, with the name referring to dense protective mountain forest. The baroque parish church dedicated to Saint Wolfgang was enlarged in 1698 from an earlier 1500 chapel. A rare cultural treasure inside the sanctuary is a sequence of twelve historic Dance of Death (Totentanz) paintings depicting the memento mori theme.

Anreise

A notable benefit of Schattwald is vignette-free road access from Germany. Motorists travel along the A7 motorway past Kempten, continuing via Sonthofen and Bad Hindelang over the Oberjoch Pass directly to Schattwald without requiring an Austrian highway toll sticker. From within Austria, the B199 leads through the Gaicht Pass from Reutte. Rail travellers arrive at Sonthofen station in Bavaria or Reutte station in Tyrol. From both directions, VVT regional bus line 120 connects regularly, with local buses free for guests holding the Tannheimer Tal card.

Tipps

During both summer and winter, the Wannenjochbahn chairlift at the village edge opens up alpine recreation. In summer, the mountain station provides access to scenic ridge trails towards Kühgundkopf and the Smugglers' Trail (Schmugglersteig), an interactive family theme walk across the border into Bavaria. In winter, the lift joins with Zöblen to form a family-oriented ski circuit with 15 kilometres of slopes. A scenic hike follows the tumbling cascades of the Stuibenbach stream up to the rustic Stuibenalpe hut (1,400 m). Additionally, Schattwald provides immediate entry onto the 140-kilometre cross-country ski network of the Tannheimer Tal.
